title: Object Lifetime
summary: Instance lifecycle: create → configure → parent (enter world) → live → destroy (or unparent). Destroy cascades to children, locks Parent forever, but does NOT sever event connections or code references — those are leaks unless you clean them.

explanation.whatItIs: Every instance has a life story, and each stage has rules — especially the end. Knowing when objects die (and what survives them) separates clean games from leaky ones.
explanation.whyItExists: Games spawn and remove thousands of objects; predictable lifetime rules keep memory and events sane.
whenToUse: Temporary objects: track every connection YOU add to them and Disconnect at death
Soft removal (Parent=nil) vs Destroy: reversibility is the difference
AncestryChanged to react to moves; ChildRemoved for death notices
whenNotToUse: Destroying to 'clean up' but leaving connections listening to the corpse
explanation.mentalModel:
```text
Instance.new ─▶ configure ─▶ .Parent = world ─▶ LIVE
                                                  │
                          ┌───────────────────────┘
                          ▼
               .Parent = nil   (parked, reusable)
               :Destroy()      (gone + descendants)
                                ├─ connections: STILL ALIVE*  ← leak!
                                └─ references in code: STILL HELD

*unless destroyed via the parent's destruction
```
tips: Own the connections you attach to short-lived objects; Disconnect in the cleanup path
Weak-ish discipline: one cleanup function per spawner
Check Memory/Performance views in Studio for growth over time
commonMistakes: Connect()-ing inside a loop to new parts without ever disconnecting — listener army
Holding tables of destroyed instances (prevents full GC)
Reusing Destroy()-ed objects later — locked Parent errors

examples.title: Clean spawn + despawn
examples.code:
local function spawnMine(position, lifetime)
    local mine = Instance.new("Part")
    mine.Size = Vector3.new(1, 1, 1)
    mine.Anchored = true
    mine.Position = position

    local connections = {}
    table.insert(connections, mine.Touched:Connect(function(hit)
        -- boom
    end))

    mine.Parent = workspace

    task.delay(lifetime, function()
        for _, c in connections do c:Disconnect() end
        mine:Destroy()
    end)
end
